messages.subject: fm_mesh_2d_inla - boundary option error
parts:
Hi all, 
I'm trying to create a mesh with two boundary regions but, in the new version of function fm_mesh_2d_inla, It seems that it does not work

This is my code

# mesh  ----
mesh <-
  fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla(
    loc = stazioni$geometry,
    boundary = list(fmesher::fm_nonconvex_hull_inla(x = puntiStivale, convex = 80000,concave = 60000),fmesher::fm_nonconvex_hull_inla(x = puntiSardegna, convex = 80000,concave = 60000) ) ,
    max.edge = c(50000, 150000) ,
    cutoff = 5000,
    offset = 10000,
    min.angle = 25
  )

I'll expect something like this figure  (This mesh was created with  function inla.mesh.2d in an older version of INLA)

 But I get this with INLA 23.11.1


My old code
inla.nonconvex.hull(points=puntiStivale, convex = 80000,concave = 50000)->stivale
#sardegna: non-convex-hull for the Sardegna monitoring sites
inla.nonconvex.hull(points = puntiSardegna, convex = 80000,concave = 50000)->isola  

mesh_modello<-inla.mesh.2d(boundary =list(stivale,isola), max.edge = c(30000,150000),cutoff=5000,offset=c(10000),min.angle = 25)

Thanks
Maria Antonietta

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] fm_mesh_2d_inla - boundary option error
parts:
Does the problem also happen if you use min.angle=21 ?

It's however not entirely clear what the two boundary objects are meant to be; are they the boundaries for mainland+Sicily and for Sardinia?
If they are, then the old code wasn't supposed to work, and the new code might simply have fixed a bug!
To build boundary object for two disconnected regions, you either need a single nonconvex hull construction, or to joint the two results into a single object.
c(bnd1, bnd2) should build a joint boundary object for two separate regions defined by bnd1 and bnd2, and you can then use
  boundary=list(c(bnd1, bnd2))
The syntax
  boundary=list(bnd1, bnd2)
means "bnd1 should be the inner boundary, and bnd2 should be the outer boundary".
I think you intended "bn1 and bn2 define the inner boundary, and I want an automatic extension as the outer boundary", which is the list(c(bnd1, bnd2)) version?

Finn

Did you also try with boundary=list(list(stivale,isola)) just as in the past?

I misremembered about how c() works for fm_segm objects. You need
boundary=list(fm_segm(c(bnd1, bn2)))
to be explicit about what you want.

Finn
